ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UK HM Treasury Consolidated List of Financial Sanctions Targets, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, and relevant BVI AML/CFT sanctions lists. All directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, agents and principal counterparties must be screened before onboarding and continuously thereafter. Politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, senior management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring. Adverse media checks and risk rating are documented and retained for at least five years under the MLR 2017 and BVI AML Regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BVI Financial Services Commission – Registry of Corporate Affairs via licensed registered agents using the eVista / e-services portal; for any UK establishment registration, Companies House online filing service (www.gov.uk/companies-house)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Latin alphabetic script of the English language; the BVI accepts English alphabet characters and does not permit Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic or other non-Latin characters unless an accepted Latin transliteration is provided. The BVI corporate name must end with an approved legal suffix such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Business Company' or 'BC'. UK establishment names must comply with Companies Act 2006 and may be in English or, for Welsh companies, in Welsh with a mandatory English suffix. Special characters and misleading glyphs are generally disallowed, and an exact transliteration statement is required where a foreign-language corporate name is used.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the BVI, a proposed name reservation is filed through a licensed registered agent. If the BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs refuses a name, the registered agent may within 14 days of the refusal notice file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar, attaching evidence of non-conflict, consent from any objecting party, or a certificate of good standing. The Registrar may refer contested cases to the High Court of the British Virgin Islands. A name reservation may be extended once for a further 30 days upon payment of the applicable statutory extension fee. For a UK establishment, if Companies House rejects a name, the applicant may within 28 days submit a formal administrative review request to Companies House with supporting submissions, and thereafter pursue judicial review in the High Court of England and Wales where the administrative decision remains adverse.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For the BVI BC, a physical registered office in the BVI at the address of the licensed registered agent is mandatory; a virtual office cannot satisfy the statutory registered-office requirement. A virtual office is, however, acceptable for operational correspondence, customer service and marketing purposes of the online collectible trading-card publishing business, and is permissible as a service address. If a UK establishment is registered, Companies House permits a virtual office service address provided it is a real and effective location for service of legal documents under section 86 of the Companies Act 2006.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified risk below 10% per annum for an online-only, unlicensed, low-risk trading-card publisher. Inspections, when conducted, are intelligence-led by the BVI Financial Services Commission or UK Companies House/HMRC and would focus on registered-office integrity, UBO records, and compliance with economic substance requirements rather than routine on-site verification of trading premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 (as amended), Part II ss. 5-12 (method of incorporation, memorandum of association, name restrictions, registered office and registered agent, articles of association, certificate of incorporation, effect of registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, Financial Services Commission of the British Virgin Islands; electronic filing through the VIRGIN online system by a BVI-licensed Registered Agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (electronic form BC1) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and the consent of the Registered Agent; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Registrar upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 imposes no minimum authorized or paid-up share capital; shares may have par value or no par value, and consideration is fixed by the Board. No statutory escrow, deposit, or capital maintenance account is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Registry be approved, ratified, and adopted in their entirety. RESOLVED, that the subscriber share subscriptions be confirmed and shares allotted and issued to the subscribers named in the Memorandum. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the Registered Agent's office and the appointment of the Registered Agent be ratified. RESOLVED, that [Director Name] and [Secretary Name] be and are hereby appointed as first Director and Company Secretary, respectively, to serve until removed. RESOLVED, that the Directors be authorized severally to open bank accounts, engage payment processors including Stripe and Authorize.Net, and execute all ancillary documents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC); online filing and registration portal via GOV.UK Government Gateway (www.gov.uk).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-UK incorporated entity such as a BVI Business Company has no automatic UK taxpayer reference. Registration obligations arise only on specified triggers: (1) Corporation Tax: if the BVI BC commences a trade in the UK through a permanent establishment, it must notify HMRC within 3 months of starting to trade and file form CT41G/CT400 or register via the online Corporation Tax service to obtain a UK Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR). (2) VAT: the entity must register for VAT and obtain a VAT registration number if it makes taxable supplies in the UK; a non-established taxable person is required to register when it makes any taxable supply in the UK, while a UK-established business can apply once annual turnover reaches the £90,000 threshold or is expected to exceed it within 30 days. Registration is through the HMRC VAT portal (form VAT1 online). (3) Customs: an EORI number (GB/EORI) must be applied for via HMRC to declare imports/exports in the UK.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The UK does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity classification election; a BVI Business Company is an opaque corporation for UK law. Relevant statutory elections and mitigation mechanisms include: (a) group relief (loss-relief) elections under CTA 2010 for 75% UK-resident group companies; (b) election to treat a UK permanent establishment as a separate enterprise for double-taxation treaty purposes; (c) transfer-pricing and capital-allowances elections; (d) VAT option to tax (waiver of exemption) for UK real estate; and (e) hybrid mismatch recharacterisation adjustments under TIOPA 2010 Part 6A, with elective treatment for certain chain and structured arrangements where administratively permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 (annual taxable turnover for UK-established businesses; non-established taxable persons must register from the first taxable supply made in the UK, subject to UK distance-selling rules and marketplace provisions)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance or digital stamping is mandated in the UK. Mandatory electronic filing and digital record-keeping apply under Making Tax Digital for VAT (MTDf); VAT returns are transmitted to HMRC using MTD-compatible software APIs. E-invoicing is accepted but is contractual and not a legal requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to a supply of goods where the supplier exports the goods from the UK (including a physical removal to a destination outside the UK) in the course of a supply to a person who is not in the UK, or from such a person to the supplier where the goods are subsequently exported; the supplier must obtain and preserve valid evidence of export (e.g., customs declaration, shipping documentation, delivery confirmation) within 3 months of the time of supply (or such extended period as HMRC allows). Offshore services directly related to exported goods may also be zero-rated under item 1/2 of Group 7, Schedule 8, VATA 1994; B2B services to overseas recipients are generally outside the scope or zero-rated under the place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (submitted through the UK Customs Declaration Service (CDS), generating a Declaration Unique Consignment Reference (DUCR))
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill/CMR consignment note for land transport)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank statement evidencing foreign exchange receipt from the export sale)
Proof of Export (PEX 3 / C88 or HMRC-approved alternative)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may retrospectively disallow zero-rating and assess VAT at the standard rate (20%) if the exported-goods evidence is insufficient or the export condition fails. Fraudulent export claims are subject to a civil penalty of up to 100% of the VAT evaded under FA 2007 Sch 24 or FA 2008 Sch 41, plus interest; dishonest evasion may be prosecuted criminally with unlimited fines and imprisonment. Clawback assessments are made under VATA 1994 s.73, with a time limit of 4 years for corrections to relevant VAT returns (20 years in cases of fraud); liability to repay any input VAT recovered in connection with the failed zero-rating also applies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England; monetary and financial stability authority with no direct foreign exchange control function in the United Kingdom.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom operates a fully liberalised current and capital account regime. There are no exchange control approvals, surrender requirements, or profit remittance authorisations for dividends, royalties, service payments, intra-group loans, or capital repatriation. Convertibility is unrestricted subject to compliance with UK anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing, sanctions, and tax transparency obligations. The only practical hurdles are banking counterparty risk appetite, accurate declaration of purpose codes on SWIFT instructions, and documentary proof of beneficial ownership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in the UK. Exporters are freely permitted to retain foreign currency proceeds in domestic or overseas bank accounts. No obligation to remit or convert export earnings exists. Statistical reporting may require completion of the Bank of England's Quarterly International Trade in Services and Investment Survey for transactions above threshold, but no surrender or conversion mandate applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: UK FCA-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) and authorised payment institutions present a viable alternative for day-to-day cross-border treasury operations. The feasibility rating is High for restricted transactional banking, including multi-currency IBANs, SWIFT-like transfers, and card acquiring. Legal constraints include: EMI status does not constitute a full banking licence; customer funds must be safeguarded in segregated accounts or covered by an insurance policy; EMIs may not lend or create credit; balances are not protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme; and higher risk jurisdictions may trigger enhanced due diligence. For the BVI Business Company, a strong economic substance narrative, certified corporate registry extracts, and a clean source-of-funds trail materially improve approval odds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: UK law does not mandate physical director attendance at bank branches to satisfy know-your-customer requirements. Remote onboarding is generally permissible using electronic identification, liveness checks, video conferencing, and certified digital copies of corporate documents. For a BVI Business Company, UK banks may nonetheless require one or all directors to attend a virtual interview, provide notarised and apostilled corporate register extracts, or undergo an introducer/referee confirmation. Physical presence is not legally mandated but may be a bank-specific policy for higher risk or complex ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BVI Business Company with bearer shares, nominee directors, or opaque ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, register of directors, register of members, certificate of good standing from the BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs, and a completed UK beneficial ownership declaration identifying all natural persons with significant control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transactions into or from sanctions-listed or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full counterparty and end-client KYC file, transactional flowcharts, commercial invoices and contracts, shipping and customs documentation, sanctions screening reports from at least two independent screening databases, and a legal opinion from a UK-qualified firm confirming no sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth insufficiently documented for initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or accountants' confirmation of the ultimate shareholder's wealth, tax returns, bank statements over the preceding 12 months, sale and purchase agreements explaining major liquidity events, and a sworn statement with supporting corroborating evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial purpose for the BVI-BC entity operating a UK trading card business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed board resolution describing the business rationale, principal commercial agreements with UK suppliers and EU distributors, evidence of physical production or logistics arrangements, intellectual property licence agreements, and a projected cash flow forecast for the first two operational years.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the BVI parent or ultimate beneficial owner to the UK operational account should be executed via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code G2 (capital transfer) or the bank-specific equivalent for equity capital contributions. The remitter must provide the BVI company's unique identifiers, certified board resolution authorising the capital injection, audited or management source-of-funds evidence, and a completed funds-received questionnaire if requested by the receiving UK bank. No exchange control notification is required. Correspondent banks will screen the transaction for financial sanctions and may request evidence that the BVI entity has sufficient economic substance or that the capital is not being used to circumvent UK tax or regulatory obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the printing and distribution of collectible trading cards should use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments, MT202 for interbank/treasury transfers, and commercial letters of credit issued by the UK account bank for major raw-material purchases. All payment instructions must include clear purpose codes such as 'Goods' with the applicable commodity code, an accurate invoice reference, and a beneficial owner certification where required. UK banks will ensure transactions are screened against consolidated sanctions lists, and the documentary trail must include supplier invoices, bills of lading or airway bills, customs declarations, and proof of shipping. Alternative clearing rails include UK Faster Payments for domestic disbursements and SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated settlements within the EEA.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (vanilla) under an ISDA 1992 Master Agreement or a bank-specific FX master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for currencies with restricted deliverability, provided the counterparty bank is authorised by the FCA
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matching long-term USD/EUR asset and liability exposures
Plain-vanilla FX swaps for liquidity management between receipt and disbursement currencies
Flexible forwards allowing early termination or extension of the settlement date

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Government Fee (Annual Licence Fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Financial Services Commission (FSC) – payable via the appointed BVI Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May each year, covering the fixed 1 June – 31 May annual period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late fee if paid after 31 May; additional penalties for extended delay; continued non-payment may trigger strike-off of the company from the BVI Register of Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Return (statutory return of members, directors, and registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Registrar of Corporate Affairs (Registry of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within nine months after the end of each financial year (e.g., FYE 31 December → due 30 September)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 200 and possible restriction of the company's Certificate of Good Standing; persistent default can result in strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UK Corporation Tax Return (Form CT600) and accounts computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 12 months after the end of the accounting period; corporation tax payment due 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GBP 100 (GBP 200 if more than 3 months late), escalating daily penalties of GBP 10 per day after 6 months; interest on underpaid tax and surcharges of 5% for late payment beyond 6 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Economic Substance Notification (ESN) – annual filing confirming relevant activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within nine months after the end of the company's financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties up to USD 20,000 for failure to file, and USD 40,000 for serious or repeated breaches; possible strike-off or capitation of the registered agent certification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for a private BVI Business Company unless it is a public company or the FSC/ITA orders an audit; for UK tax purposes, HMRC does not mandate an independent audit, but accounts must be prepared to support the CT return and may be audited if the company exceeds the UK parent/group thresholds (aggregate turnover > £102m, aggregate balance sheet > £51m) and is a UK-resident group member.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (as issued by the IASB) for BVI financial records and annual return preparation; UK tax submissions prepared under IFRS or UK GAAP (FRS 101/102) as permitted by HMRC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain the beneficial ownership register and report any change to the BVI FSC via the Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) system. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation; the BVI Annual Return (due within 9 months of year-end) must include the current members and directors. The registered agent conducts annual due diligence to confirm UBO details.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,800 per year (BVI registered agent and registered office service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 10,000 (if external audit is required; optional for private BVI BC)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 April 2024; 19% small-profits rate for profits at or below £50,000; marginal relief where associated-company adjusted profits are between £50,000 and £250,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday; available structural reliefs: 100% full expensing for qualifying plant and machinery; 100% Annual Investment Allowance up to £1,000,000; Patent Box 10% for qualifying patent and digitally-embedded IP profits; R&D relief including merged expenditure credit (20% from 1 April 2024) for qualifying manufacturing innovation; creative-industry tax reliefs where design-led collectible-card publishing qualifies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CT600 Corporation Tax Return and supplementary pages (including CT600A etc.) submitted through HMRC-recognised third-party software via the HMRC online filing service / Government Gateway; CT600 XML and company accounts/tax computation must be submitted as XBRL; Making Tax Digital for Corporation Tax becomes mandatory for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 April 2026.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one return per accounting period with a maximum period of 12 months; shorter periods require a short-period CT600 and apportioned reliefs.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return filing is due 12 months from the end of the accounting period; self-assessment tax is due and payable 9 months and 1 day after the period end; large companies (UK taxable profits above £1,500,000) pay by quarterly instalment payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered number, registered address, tax district reference, jurisdiction of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a BVI Business Company, state jurisdiction BVI and insert UK permanent establishment address if one exists; if no UK PE, do not file CT600 unless HMRC has served notice or a UK tax liability arises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the statutory accounting period of the non-resident company; UK PE accounts should be drawn to the same period end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from trading, investment income and sundry income for the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to the UK permanent establishment; portfolio dividends from UK companies are generally excluded for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Wholly and exclusively incurred revenue expenses, apportioned head-office costs and depreciation disallowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The UK PE must use arm's-length recharge and expense allocation; intra-group charges must satisfy UK transfer-pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted trading profit before capital allowances and reliefs after UK GAAP and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use UK GAAP/IFRS accounts of the UK branch; apply the ‘force of attraction’ rule only where tax treaty permits; no treaty means allocate only attributable profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trading and non-trading losses carried forward into the current accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward is restricted to 50% of the excess profit over the £5,000,000 statutory allowance for large groups; non-resident PE losses must have arisen in the same UK trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profits after loss relief, deductions and exemptions, before applying corporation tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are taxed on UK-source trading profits, UK property business income and chargeable gains on UK assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed by applying the 19% or 25% rate, or marginal relief, to taxable total profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the rate for associated companies; include UK PE profit after apportionment; no turbo effect from BVI zero-tax status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, group relief, R&D credits, and patent box relief claimed in computing liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because no UK-BVI DTA applies, a BVI-recipient company may only rely on unilateral UK relief if a foreign tax was charged on the same income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount of Corporation Tax payable after instalments, deductions at source and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the UK bank details for repayment are provided; payments are made to HMRC Cumbernauld by electronic funds transfer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing – £100 automatic charge; additional £100 if filing is more than three months late; tax-geared penalties of 10% of unpaid tax where six months late and a further 10% at twelve months; maximum up to 20% where a final determination has been made. HMRC may also impose daily penalties up to £60 per day for a continued failure. Late payment interest is applied at Bank of England base rate plus 2.5%; non-payment can lead to enforcement action and criminal prosecution in deliberate cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (UK companies generally pay dividends without withholding tax; no statutory dividend withholding is imposed on ordinary distributions to non-resident shareholders).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The UK and BVI do not have a comprehensive double taxation agreement; therefore a BVI Business Company cannot file a UK tax-treaty relief form for dividends, interest or royalties. Where a treaty alliance exists between the UK and the payer's residence country, the administrative protocol is: verify treaty entitlement; obtain an original tax residence certificate (TRC) from the relevant revenue authority; submit the TRC and a treaty relief declaration to the UK business before payment; and, where tax has been withheld, claim refund through HMRC or self-assessment. For BVI, only unilateral relief is available and only if foreign tax was suffered on the same income; the BVI International Tax Authority's tax-residency certificate is ineffective for UK WHT reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: UK statutory rate is 20% withholding on UK-source annual interest and patent royalties paid to non-resident companies; from 1 April 2019, royalties for the use of IP and similar rights connected with a UK trade are also within the 20% withholding scope. There is no UK-BVI treaty, so the 20% is final and cannot be reduced to a treaty rate; UK-dividend payments have no withholding, and BVI does not impose withholding on outward payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The UK does not impose a simple local-currency local-file threshold. Large companies generally require OECD-aligned TP documentation; a company is large unless it satisfies at least two of the three UK companies-act size conditions (turnover ≤ £200m, balance-sheet assets ≤ £1bn, employees ≤250). A Country-by-Country Report is mandatory where group consolidated revenue is at least €750 million (approx. £641m), and the relevant UK entity must file the UK CbCR return through HMRC.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: UK law will disallow artificial profit treatment if the BVI BC has management and control, or a fixed place of business, in the UK, resulting in a UK permanent establishment and diverted-profits assessment under the Diverted Profits Tax (25% on profits displaced offshore). At BVI level, the BVI Business Company remains subject to the BVI Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act and must file an economic substance return. A non-resident BVI BC must prove its tax residence in the UK and must comply with UK CT; an entity claiming pure holding status but actually licensing or distributing collectible trading-card IP will be treated as carrying on a relevant activity where substantive commercial decisions are made in the UK, and will face both HMRC and BVI International Tax Authority scrutiny.
